title: Fraud Risk Assessment and Control Design
summary: Building a fraud risk assessment that covers products, channels, customers and third parties, and turning it into a proportionate prevention and detection control framework.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Building a fraud risk assessment that covers products, channels, customers and third parties, and turning it into a proportionate prevention and detection control framework.
Learning Objectives: Conduct a fraud risk assessment across products, channels and customer segments
Design preventive and detective controls proportionate to the assessed risk
Embed fraud risk in product design, change and third-party oversight
Syllabus: Inherent risk, control effectiveness and residual risk for fraud
Fraud risk in product design, onboarding journeys and new payment channels
Balancing friction, customer experience and loss prevention
Exercise: fraud risk assessment for a new payment product
Intended Audience: Fraud prevention, fraud operations and investigations teams
Payments operations, customer service and complaints staff who handle suspected fraud cases
Compliance, financial crime and risk staff, and managers accountable for fraud outcomes
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of fraud, payments operations or financial crime compliance is helpful. No technical background in data analytics is required.
Core Reading: FATF, Opportunities and Challenges of New Technologies for AML/CFT (2021)
G20/OECD High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection (2022)
CPMI, Fast Payments: Enhancing the Speed and Availability of Retail Payments (2016)
